# Boundary to interior: predicting volume fields from the surface {#sec-interior}

**On the one task that asks for the flow rather than the wall pressure,
how an architecture treats an interior point decides the result. ISLA's
reference configuration admits its interior queries as interacting tokens
and gives them the signed distance to the wall, the input GeoTransolver's
volume configuration receives. On the 48 DrivAerML validation cars, in
float32, it scores 0.0550 on interior pressure, 0.0782 on velocity and
0.1005 on eddy viscosity against GeoTransolver-volume's 0.0513, 0.1070 and
0.0879: 7% behind on pressure, 27% ahead on velocity and 14% behind on
eddy viscosity (arm ÷ GeoTransolver-volume 1.07, 0.73 and 1.14), at a third
of the parameters (@sec-nb-relint-verdict). Decode the queries passively
instead, so that a prediction at one point never depends on which other
points are asked for, and ISLA is 3.1x behind on pressure.**
The reporting instrument for every number in this chapter is float32
inference; the rule and its reason are stated once in @sec-metrics, and a
table or caption that uses bfloat16 says so.
The passive contract is worth keeping for a surrogate queried on arbitrary
probe sets, and on DrivAerML the complete passive configuration as built (a
separate four-block read decoder, no signed-distance input) costs 3.1x in
interior pressure error; a passive decode at matched depth and inputs costs
1.43x (@sec-interior-query-independence). The interacting configuration's
prediction depends on the joint query set: on the similarity-gauge interior
variant, pressure error at the training count of 10,000 queries is 0.0547,
at 2,000 queries 0.0753 and at 20,000 queries 0.0531, so the model is
deployed at the count it was trained at (@sec-interior-companion;
@sec-nb-qcount-verdict). The passive deficit ratio is smallest at the wall
and grows with distance from it, but almost all of the excess squared error
on the sampled points (95%) lies within the first 5 cm of the wall, so the
ratio's growth does not by itself name a missing mechanism
(@sec-interior-distance). Two attempts to supply interior context without
breaking the passive contract fail: off-surface latent tokens along anchor
normals make ISLA worse, and the exact-kernel MeshTransformer's
boundary-integral decoder is 9.7x behind (0.76M parameters against 27.6M)
because potential flow is the wrong prior for a separated wake
(@sec-interior-negatives). Interaction among the queries is what closes the
gap: query tokens without the signed distance trail GeoTransolver-volume by
1.2x on pressure, 1.3x on velocity and 1.6x on eddy viscosity; the signed
distance as a query input moves the same variant to 1.08x, 0.75x and 1.27x
(three seeds, @sec-nb-qtsdf-seed44), and the reference frame with the
corrected boundary measure takes eddy viscosity to 1.14x.

## The task {#sec-interior-task}

A surrogate that returns only wall pressure answers one engineering
question (forces); one that returns the volume flow answers the rest
(wake structure, cooling-flow paths, where separation begins). The task
here is the second, in its strictest form: predict the fields inside the
fluid domain from the vehicle surface alone. ISLA is held to that form.
GeoTransolver's volume configuration is not: it never sees the surface
sample, and takes instead, at every interior point, the signed distance to
the full-resolution vehicle surface and its gradient (the *Resources*
paragraph below), which is the surface information in a different, denser
form.

**Data.** DrivAerML (@sec-datasets), the 435-car training split and the
48-car validation split used for every DrivAerML comparison in this book.
Each car contributes a sample of the vehicle boundary (cell centroids,
unit normals, cell areas as measure weights) and 10,000 interior query
points sampled from the CFD volume mesh. The volume dataset exists in two
boundary variants, and the table below names which one each ISLA arm
trained on. In the first, the reader applies a 10,000-cell and then a
10,000-point subsample to every boundary and the point cut keeps only the
cells whose three vertices all survive, so about 365 cells per car
(341–395 on four validation cars) reach the model; in the second the
boundary is subsampled by cells and the nominal 10,000 cells reach it,
with the cell measure corrected so that it sums to the surface area.
GeoTransolver's volume configuration reads no boundary and is the same on
both. The choice does not move the result: the similarity-gauge interior
variant scores 0.0553 / 0.0804 / 0.1109 (pressure / velocity / eddy
viscosity, three seeds) on the 365-cell variant and 0.0550 / 0.0789 /
0.1142 on the 10,000-cell variant, within the preregistered 3% null band
on every field (@sec-nb-v0surf-verdict; results/relint2_reduction_2026-09-14.json).
On this task the interior result is carried by the interacting queries and
the signed distance, and 27x more surface information adds nothing
measurable. The volume mesh holds 150–166 million points per car, so the
query sample covers roughly 6 × 10⁻⁵ of it, and it is overwhelmingly
near-wall (median distance to the surface 5 mm; @sec-interior-distance
returns to this). Targets at each query point are the static pressure, the
three velocity components, and the turbulent eddy viscosity ν_t. The
interior sample is bit-identical across every trained run.

**Metric.** For one car and one field f, the relative L2 error is

$$
\varepsilon = \frac{\lVert \hat f - f \rVert_2}{\lVert f \rVert_2}
$$

over the 10,000 interior sample points, where f is the field in training
normalisation: pressure as the coefficient C_p = (p − p_∞)/q_∞ with
p_∞ = 0, velocity as U/|U_∞| with the freestream mean included, Frobenius
norm over the three components, and eddy viscosity as the standardized
(ν_t − 4.8×10⁻⁴)/9.4×10⁻⁴, scored *before* inverse normalization. The
viscosity denominator is therefore the norm of a mean-subtracted field, and
an eddy-viscosity value of 0.10 is not a 10% error in physical ν_t;
orderings between arms under this frozen metric stand, but a ratio of
arithmetic means need not survive a different centering. The number
reported for an arm is the arithmetic mean of ε over the 48 validation
cars; where a table cell is a ratio, the numerator is the named arm and the
denominator is GeoTransolver-volume on the same 48 cars, so a ratio above
1 means the arm is less accurate than GeoTransolver-volume. This is the
reverse of the convention in the rest of the book, where ratios are
baseline ÷ ISLA and a value above 1 favours ISLA; it is used here because
GeoTransolver-volume is the denominator for seven arms at once. Velocity's
denominator includes the freestream and is never small; pressure is a
gauge quantity whose denominator can be tiny far from the body
(@sec-interior-distance).

**Protocol.** 500 epochs, learning rate 1e-3 for every arm (no per-arm
tuning on this task), bfloat16 training, no augmentation, two seeds (42
and 43) unless a row says three; float32 evaluation at the training count
of 10,000 queries.

**Resources and inputs.** The arms are not resource-matched, and they do
not see the same inputs; both facts are read from each run's training
log and configuration
(results/v0_interior_resources_2026-09-07.json). Every memory figure in this
chapter is the training logger's peak `torch.cuda.memory_reserved()`, one
instrument for all arms here but a different one from the allocated-memory
figures of @sec-mt2-cost. GeoTransolver's volume
configuration has **27.6M parameters** and peaks at **8.8 GB** per GPU: it is
the surface configuration's 12-layer, 256-wide backbone (@sec-baselines)
plus local ball-query features at six radii from 0.01 to 5.0
nondimensional units, which the surface configuration does not use. Its
tokens are the **10,000 interior points only**; the boundary surface sample
is not consumed. Each interior token carries its coordinates, the signed
distance to the full-resolution vehicle surface and that distance's
gradient (the unit normal of the nearest wall), and the freestream enters
globally as the unit direction; the geometry encoder runs on the interior
point cloud. Fed the physical freestream velocity (38.9 m/s) instead,
GeoTransolver-volume scores 0.0514 / 0.1088 / 0.0879, within 2% of the
unit-drive 0.0513 / 0.1070 / 0.0879 on every field
(@sec-nb-udrv-int-verdict), so the interior ordering does not depend on the
input-scale requirement of @sec-part-baseline. ISLA with query tokens has
**8.9M parameters** (the surface configuration's count, @sec-mt2) and
peaks at **6.0 GB** on the stored-activation path; with the exact
activation recompute and the compiled geometry region of @sec-mt2-cost its
peak allocated memory is 2.5 GiB at 0.83x the step time
(results/isla_qt_cost_2026-09-07.json). Its per-step time at this size is
0.28 s, about five times GeoTransolver-volume's 0.04–0.05 s, because its
per-slice geometry spans all 20,000 tokens. ISLA in its passive-decode
configuration has **9.9M parameters** (8.9M plus four read blocks) and
peaks at **4.9 GB**; it consumes the surface tokens with normals and
areas, the freestream direction, and at each interior query its position
and, in the SDF-gradient arm, the same wall normal GeoTransolver-volume
receives, but not the distance itself. The latent-volume-token arm has
10.0M parameters at 5.8 GB; the exact-kernel MeshTransformer 0.76M at
4.0 GB. Three differences therefore separate GeoTransolver-volume from
ISLA's passive decode on this task: interaction among the query tokens,
the signed-distance input, and 2.8x the parameters with local features.
The passive decode's 3.1x bounds the price of ISLA's contracts as ISLA is
built; the query-token arms isolate the first two differences one at a
time (@sec-interior-results).

### Query independence as a first-class property {#sec-interior-query-independence}

In ISLA's passive configuration an interior query is never a token. The
encoder sees the surface only; interior queries are decoded passively, by read blocks
(@sec-mt2-forward) that read the slice states and the boundary tokens
and write nothing back, so a prediction at one interior point is
independent of the other interior points queried (verified in fp64 to
10⁻¹², @sec-query-independence). This is a property of the interior
decode: ISLA's surface predictions in this book come from a configuration
whose heads read the interacting encoder tokens, and do not share it. A
user who asks for one streamline, a plane, or the whole domain gets the
same answer at every shared point, at a cost linear in the points asked
for. GeoTransolver-volume's queries are tokens, so its answer at a point
depends on the other points requested with it.

The passive route was tested at matched depth and inputs on the
similarity-gauge interior variant: a decode that reads through twelve
blocks from an interacting support set of 5,000 surface tokens carrying
the signed distance, with 5,000 passive queries, scores 0.078 / 0.107 /
0.269 (pressure, velocity, eddy viscosity; two seeds) against 0.055 /
0.080 / 0.112 for the interacting query-token configuration, 1.43x, 1.34x
and 2.41x, past the preregistered pressure falsifier of 0.060. Twelve read
blocks against four buy 13% on pressure and the support set 12%; neither
moves eddy viscosity. The interacting queries therefore provide
computation at the requested points through every encoder layer rather
than geometric context, and the passive route is closed for ISLA at
matched depth
(`research/transfer_program/studies/computational_support/d1_verdict_2026-09-10.json`).
The request-size dependence of the interacting decode is partly a
training-distribution effect and partly intrinsic: the same variant
trained with the interior request size drawn per sample between 2,000 and
20,000 points (@sec-nb-qcount-prereg) reduces the dependence by about 40%
(the 2,000-request penalty on pressure falls from +38% to +24%, on
velocity from +59% to +31%, on eddy viscosity from +49% to +31%, and the
2,000-request prediction itself improves from 0.0753 to 0.0703) at a 3.7%
accuracy cost at the training count (0.0567 against 0.0547), and still
improves at 20,000. Query-count consistency is therefore an architectural
question, with count augmentation as a partial and costly mitigation
(`results/qcount_reduction_2026-09-11.json`, @sec-nb-qcount-verdict).

### How each architecture treats an interior point

*GeoTransolver.* The interior points are the tokens. Each carries its
coordinates, the signed distance to the wall and the wall normal at the
nearest surface point; the tokens are routed to slices and attend through
the same layers as in the surface task, so an interior token gathers
context from the other interior tokens before it is decoded, and its
knowledge of the geometry comes from the signed-distance inputs and from
ball-query features over neighbouring interior points at six radii, not
from surface tokens, which this configuration does not receive.

*ISLA.* The passive decoder builds every query-side invariant from the
query position q, the freestream direction d, and a unit normal n̂ at
the query. Lengths need two conventions kept apart. The recipe stores
coordinates nondimensionalized by the dataset's per-case reference
length L_ref, which is 5 m for every DrivAerML car; the passive arms then
measure q from the centroid in *gauge units*, dividing by a constant gauge
of 8.0 in those nondimensional units (40 m physical on DrivAerML). The
invariants are
{|q|, log|q|, q̂·d, q̂·n̂, n̂·d}. Surface points have normals; interior
points do not, so a normal has to be constructed. Two constructions are
measured.

The first is a *soft-assigned proxy normal*. Each slice s of the encoder
has an equivariant anchor: a measure-weighted mean position z_s and a
mean normal m_s. The query is softly assigned to anchors by distance and
inherits their normals,

$$
\hat n(q) = \operatorname{normalize}\!\Big(\sum_s a_s(q)\, m_s\Big),
\qquad
a_s(q) = \operatorname{softmax}_s\!\big(-|q - z_s|^2 / \rho^2\big),
$$

with ρ = 0.25 gauge units (2.0 nondimensional units, 10 m on
DrivAerML). It is exactly SE(3)-covariant, smooth,
defined everywhere and parameter-free; every read block and the vector
head run unchanged.

The second is the *signed-distance-field gradient*: the data pipeline
computes, for every interior point, the distance to the full-resolution
vehicle surface and its gradient, which is the unit normal of the nearest
wall. Passed as the query normal it overrides the proxy; it is equally
covariant and carries information about the local wall geometry that the
proxy does not.

*The exact-kernel MeshTransformer, an earlier design of this program.*
A one-layer attention encoder reads the boundary sample; its decoder
then evaluates the exact double-layer and single-layer Laplace kernels
from every boundary panel to the query, weighted by learned,
operator-conditioned densities, so an interior prediction is a
discretized boundary integral rather than a learned interpolation. Its
contracts, similarity equivariance and, when declared, linearity in the
drive, are exact for potential flow, where these kernels are the
Green's-function representation of the solution, and the decoder is
query-independent by construction. The arm trained here drops the
surface-trace terms so that every interior output is the boundary
integral alone. The rest of this chapter calls it the exact-kernel
decoder.

### ISLA with query tokens {#sec-interior-query-tokens}

*ISLA, interacting mode.* The same architecture admits its interior
queries into the encoder as tokens. Each query is seeded with the
invariants of its position, its wall normal (the SDF gradient) and the
freestream direction, exactly as a surface token is, plus a learned
type embedding, and enters the measure-weighted slice routing with a
learned weight relative to the surface measure; the twelve slice layers
then run over surface and query tokens together, and the heads read the
query tokens. In the reference configuration the position enters only
through relative geometry (the frame-free relative frame with the
total-measure scale, @sec-mt2); in the similarity-gauge variant it is
measured from the Horvitz–Thompson centroid in units of the RMS radius.
Either way every invariant is a function of relative geometry, so the
prediction stays rotation- and translation-covariant by construction (and
scale-covariant; verified to roundoff in fp64, @sec-mt2-contracts). What is
given up is query independence: a query's prediction depends on the other
queries in the batch, as GeoTransolver-volume's does, and, because each
query's routing weight is a learned multiple of the *geometric mean* of
the source weights, on how finely the surface is sampled and how many
queries are asked for (splitting every surface cell in two at half the
area moves a small random model's output by 4–9%, @sec-mt2-contracts); on
the trained checkpoint the dependence on the number of co-queried points
is measured in @sec-interior-companion. Nothing else changes: 8.9M
parameters, the surface configuration's hyperparameters, no local
features. The query carries the signed distance as a scalar input in
every arm named "+ signed distance"; the arm named "SDF-gradient normal
only" receives the wall normal but not the distance.

## Results {#sec-interior-results}

**ISLA's reference configuration, with its interior queries admitted as
interacting tokens and given the signed distance to the wall, is 27% more
accurate than GeoTransolver-volume on interior velocity (0.0782 against
0.1070, a ratio of 0.73), 7% less accurate on interior pressure (0.0550
against 0.0513, 1.07) and 14% less accurate on eddy viscosity (0.1005
against 0.0879, 1.14), at a third of the parameters and with the two
models' inputs matched (@sec-nb-relint-verdict). The similarity-gauge
variant of the same configuration matches it on pressure and velocity and
trails on eddy viscosity (1.27x on three seeds); without the signed
distance the query tokens trail GeoTransolver-volume on every field (1.2x,
1.3x, 1.6x); the passive, query-independent decode is 3.1x behind on
pressure, and no passive construction tried closes that gap.**
@tbl-interior gives the arithmetic-mean relative L2 over the 48 validation
cars for each arm, both seeds, and the ratio to GeoTransolver-volume;
@fig-interior-arms draws the pressure column.

| arm | boundary variant | parameters | pressure (per seed) | velocity | ν_t | pressure ratio, arm ÷ GeoTransolver-volume |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver-volume: interior points as interacting tokens with signed distance and wall normal as inputs; no surface tokens; unit freestream direction | none | 27.6M | 0.0513 (0.0512 / 0.0514) | 0.1070 | 0.0879 | 1.0 |
| ISLA, reference configuration: query tokens + signed distance on the relative frame with the total-measure scale and the corrected boundary measure | 10,000 cells | 8.9M | 0.0550 (0.0545 / 0.0556) | 0.0782 | 0.1005 | 1.07 |
| ISLA, similarity-gauge variant: query tokens + signed distance | 10,000 cells | 8.9M | 0.0550 (0.0548 / 0.0552) | 0.0789 | 0.1142 | 1.07 |
| ISLA, similarity-gauge variant: query tokens + signed distance (three seeds) | 365 cells | 8.9M | 0.0553 (0.0547 / 0.0547 / 0.0564) | 0.0804 | 0.1109 | 1.08 |
| ISLA, similarity-gauge variant: query tokens, SDF-gradient normal only | 365 cells | 8.9M | 0.0615 (0.0613 / 0.0617) | 0.1390 | 0.1416 | 1.20 |
| ISLA, passive decode from the surface tokens, SDF-gradient normal at the query | 365 cells | 9.9M | 0.157 (0.165 / 0.149) | 0.305 | 0.374 | 3.1 |
| ISLA, passive decode, proxy normal | 365 cells | 9.9M | 0.190 (0.191 / 0.188) | 0.332 | 0.398 | 3.7 |
| exact-kernel decoder, double-layer | 365 cells | 0.76M | 0.496 (0.499 / 0.493) | 0.549 | 0.727 | 9.7 |

: Interior relative L2 error on the 48 DrivAerML validation cars in
float32 (arithmetic mean over cars, then over seeds; per-seed pressure in
parentheses), 10,000 interior queries per car, 500 epochs, learning rate
1e-3. The boundary-variant column names which boundary sample the ISLA and
exact-kernel arms consumed (@sec-interior-task); GeoTransolver-volume reads
none. Ratio = arm ÷ GeoTransolver-volume, so a value above 1 means less
accurate than GeoTransolver-volume; this is the reverse of the book's usual
baseline ÷ ISLA convention. The arms are not resource-matched and do not
receive the same inputs (parameters and peak per-GPU training memory in the
*Resources and inputs* paragraph of @sec-interior-task,
results/v0_interior_resources_2026-09-07.json). Seed spreads are 1–3% of
the mean on pressure for the query-token arms and up to 10% for the
passive arms, so every ratio is resolved. Sources:
`results/relint2_reduction_2026-09-14.json` (GeoTransolver-volume and the
three query-token + signed-distance rows) and
`results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_interior_2026-09-09.json` (the remaining
rows). {#tbl-interior}

```{python}
#| label: fig-interior-arms
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Interior pressure error by architecture on the 48 DrivAerML validation
#|   cars, float32. Bars are the seed mean of the per-car arithmetic-mean
#|   relative L2 error; the dots on each bar are the individual seeds
#|   (filled = seed 42, open = seed 43, grey-filled = seed 44, same x).
#|   Labels above the bars give the ratio to GeoTransolver-volume (arm ÷
#|   GeoTransolver-volume; above 1 means less accurate than
#|   GeoTransolver-volume). How to read this: it shows the pressure column
#|   of the table only; velocity and eddy viscosity rank the arms
#|   identically except among the query-token arms (with the signed distance
#|   every ISLA variant leads GeoTransolver-volume on velocity, 0.73–0.75x,
#|   and trails on eddy viscosity, 1.14x for the reference configuration
#|   and 1.27–1.30x for the similarity-gauge variant; without it 1.3x and
#|   1.6x), and are not drawn. Data:
#|   results/relint2_reduction_2026-09-14.json (GeoTransolver-volume and
#|   the query-token + signed-distance arms) and
#|   results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_interior_2026-09-09.json (the rest).
#| code-fold: true
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib as mpl
# book palette (mirrors figures.py without importing it: that module
# switches matplotlib to Agg, which suppresses inline output here)
BLUE, RED, PURPLE = "#2a78d6", "#e34948", "#7b4fb3"
INK, INK2, MUTED, GRID, BASELINE = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#898781", "#e1e0d9", "#c3c2b7"
mpl.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 110, "font.size": 10, "axes.edgecolor": BASELINE,
                     "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID,
                     "xtick.color": MUTED, "ytick.color": MUTED, "xtick.labelcolor": INK2,
                     "ytick.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.spines.top": False,
                     "axes.spines.right": False, "legend.frameon": False})

rel = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" / "relint2_reduction_2026-09-14.json"))
fp32 = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" / "fp32_reeval" / "fp32_shift_interior_2026-09-09.json"))["runs"]
def seeds_fp32(family):
    return [fp32[f"{family}_seed{s}"]["fields"]["pressure_l2"]["fp32_mean"] for s in (42, 43)]
arms = [
    ("GeoTransolver-\nvolume", rel["gt_vol_unit"]["pressure_l2"]["seeds"], RED),
    ("ISLA reference\nquery tokens + SDF\n10,000 cells", rel["relint2"]["pressure_l2"]["seeds"], BLUE),
    ("ISLA sim. gauge\nquery tokens + SDF\n10,000 cells", rel["ref_surf10k_gauge"]["pressure_l2"]["seeds"], BLUE),
    ("ISLA sim. gauge\nquery tokens + SDF\n365 cells", rel["ref_365_gauge"]["pressure_l2"]["seeds"], BLUE),
    ("ISLA sim. gauge\nquery tokens\nno SDF", seeds_fp32("v0_isla_qt_sdf"), BLUE),
    ("ISLA passive\nSDF-gradient\nnormal", seeds_fp32("v0_mt2_int_sdf"), BLUE),
    ("ISLA passive\nproxy normal", seeds_fp32("v0_mt2_int"), BLUE),
    ("exact-kernel\ndecoder", seeds_fp32("v0_mt1k_vol"), PURPLE),
]
means = [statistics.mean(v) for _, v, _ in arms]
gt = means[0]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11.0, 4.8))
x = range(len(arms))
ax.bar(x, means, width=0.58, color=[c for _, _, c in arms], alpha=0.85, zorder=2)
fills = (INK, "white", MUTED)  # seed 42, 43, 44
for i, (_, vals, c) in enumerate(arms):
    for v, mfc in zip(vals, fills):
        ax.plot([i], [v], marker="o", ms=6, mfc=mfc, mec=INK, mew=1.0, ls="none", zorder=4)
    r = means[i] / gt
    ax.text(i, means[i] + 0.012, f"{means[i]:.3f}\n{r:.2f}x" if r < 1.5 else f"{means[i]:.3f}\n{r:.1f}x",
            ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9, color=INK2)
ax.set_xticks(list(x))
ax.set_xticklabels([n for n, _, _ in arms], fontsize=8)
ax.set_ylabel("interior pressure rel-L2, mean over 48 cars [–]")
ax.set_ylim(0, max(means) * 1.25)
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Three things in the table carry the section. First, the query-token rows:
the same ISLA, with its interior queries allowed to interact, comes within
1.2x of GeoTransolver-volume on pressure with the wall normal alone, and
within 1.07–1.08x with the signed distance added, on either frame and
either boundary variant. Second, the ordering of the two passive
constructions: the SDF-gradient normal beats the proxy normal by 1.2x on
pressure and by 7–9% on velocity and eddy viscosity, so a true wall normal
at the query is better information than a covariant blend of anchor
normals. Third, the size of what the passive decode leaves: even with the
better normal it is 3.1x behind on pressure, 2.9x on velocity and 4.2x on
eddy viscosity, and the query-token rows show that this remainder is
interaction, not the normal. The exact-kernel decoder at 9.7x is taken up
in @sec-interior-negatives.

The comparison between GeoTransolver-volume and the passive decode is
between each architecture's natural interior mode, not a matched-mechanism
ablation, and the two modes differ in three ways at once
(@sec-interior-task): GeoTransolver-volume's interior tokens interact with
each other where ISLA's passive queries only read what the surface-centred
slices hold; GeoTransolver-volume receives the signed distance to the wall
at every query where the passive decode receives at most the wall normal;
and GeoTransolver-volume has 2.8x the parameters, with local features ISLA
lacks. The 3.1x bounds the price of ISLA's contracts as ISLA is built; it
does not say which difference carries it. The query-token rows take the
differences one at a time. Admitting the queries as interacting tokens,
with the same wall-normal input as the passive arm and no signed-distance
value, takes pressure from 3.1x to 1.2x, so the complete interacting
configuration accounts for most of the pressure gap without the
signed-distance input or the 2.8x parameters. It does not isolate
interaction as such: the passive arm decodes its queries through a separate
four-block read decoder, while the query-token arm sends them through the
twelve encoder blocks with a token-type embedding and a routing weight. The
passive decode at matched depth and inputs of
@sec-interior-query-independence closes that gap in the evidence: with
twelve read blocks, an interacting support set and the signed distance, the
passive route still costs 1.43x on pressure and 2.41x on eddy viscosity, so
the price is interaction at the requested points. What interaction alone
does not close is velocity (1.3x) and eddy viscosity (1.6x), the two fields
most tied to distance from the wall, which is the second difference. The
signed distance as a query input measures it: on the similarity-gauge
variant, pressure error falls 11% (to 1.08x GeoTransolver-volume), velocity
43% (to 0.75x) and eddy viscosity 21% (to 1.27x), so the input is worth
most on the distance-dominated fields, as expected. The third difference,
GeoTransolver-volume's 2.8x parameters and six-radius local features, is
what it still has, and eddy viscosity is the one field where that still
shows; @sec-interior-open takes it up at matched parameters.

## Dependence on the query cloud {#sec-interior-companion}

**The interacting configuration's answer at a point depends on how many
other points are asked for with it, and the dependence is large below the
training query count.** Because the queries are tokens that route through
the same slices as the surface, and because each query's routing weight is
tied to the source measure in a way that also scales with the query count
(@sec-interior-query-tokens), a prediction at one interior point is a
function of the whole request. In float32 on the similarity-gauge variant
(query tokens + signed distance, 365-cell boundary, two seeds), the recipe
metric at 2,000 queries per car is 0.0753 / 0.1266 / 0.1663 (pressure /
velocity / eddy viscosity), at the training count of 10,000 it is 0.0547 /
0.0796 / 0.1116, and at 20,000 it is 0.0531 / 0.0771 / 0.1097
(`results/qcount_reduction_2026-09-11.json`, @sec-nb-qcount-verdict): a
+38% pressure penalty at a fifth of the training count and a 3% gain at
twice it. The effect at fixed points was measured on the seed-42 checkpoint
of the same variant on four validation cars: 1,000 fixed sentinel points,
drawn from the recipe's own interior sample, are predicted alone, with
1,000 companions, with 9,000 (the training count of 10,000 queries), and
with 39,000, in the recipe's inference precision (bfloat16) and in float32
(results/isla_qt_companion_dependence_2026-09-08.json). The readout is the
relative L2 change of the sentinel predictions against the training-count
run, and the error of the sentinel predictions against the truth.

| Queries in the request | Change of the sentinel prediction vs. 10,000 (pressure / ν_t / velocity) | Pressure error at the sentinels | ν_t error | Velocity error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 (sentinels alone) | 0.100 / 0.348 / 0.142 | 0.110 | 0.362 | 0.163 |
| 2,000 | 0.051 / 0.181 / 0.090 | 0.077 | 0.197 | 0.124 |
| 10,000 (training count) | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.062 | 0.080 | 0.091 |
| 40,000 | 0.029 / 0.048 / 0.045 | 0.056 | 0.084 | 0.089 |
| Passive configuration, any count (float32) | 0.000 / 0.000 / 0.000 | 0.188 | 0.400 | 0.345 |

: Companion-query dependence of the trained ISLA similarity-gauge variant
(query tokens + signed distance, seed 42), bfloat16 inference, mean over
four validation cars (run_112, run_115, run_118, run_129); relative L2 in
the recipe's normalized target space. Within-model changes under one
instrument; the absolute errors are bfloat16 values on four cars and are
not the float32 48-car means of @tbl-interior. The passive configuration
(SDF-gradient normal arm) is the control: its predictions at the sentinels
are identical to float32 roundoff whatever else is queried. Data:
results/isla_qt_companion_dependence_2026-09-08.json. {#tbl-interior-companion}

Read against the chapter's headline: the reference configuration's pressure
deficit to GeoTransolver-volume is 0.004 in absolute relative L2 (0.0550
against 0.0513) and its velocity lead 0.029. Querying 2,000 points instead
of 10,000 costs 0.021 on pressure and 0.047 on velocity in float32, more
than either margin; querying 20,000 gains 0.002 on each. So the standings
hold at the operating point the model was trained at, and they are not a
property of the model at arbitrary request sizes: a surrogate built from
this configuration is queried in batches of at least the training count.
Training over a range of counts reduces the dependence by about 40% and
does not remove it, at a 3.7% cost at the training count
(@sec-interior-query-independence); a query-mass convention that does not
scale with the count is described in @sec-mt2-contracts and the trained
checkpoints use the count-dependent one. GeoTransolver-volume's queries
are tokens too and its dependence was not measured on the full-data
checkpoints. Splitting the sentinels into two halves with the same 9,000
companions (a natural chunking) changes the prediction by 0.4–0.7% in
float32; in bfloat16 the change is 2–4%, most of it autocast numerics
rather than structure. The near-identity of the passive control (0.000 in
float32, under 1% in bfloat16 from autocast alone) confirms that the
harness measures the model and that query independence, where the
architecture promises it, holds on trained weights.

## Where the deficit lives {#sec-interior-distance}

**The passive decode's error *ratio* to GeoTransolver-volume is smallest at
the wall and grows with distance from it; its *excess error* is almost
entirely at the wall.** The two readings are of the same numbers and
neither identifies a missing mechanism. Summing the per-band squared errors
of the passive SDF-normal arm and of GeoTransolver-volume over the 48 cars
and two seeds, 94.6% of ISLA's excess pressure squared error over
GeoTransolver-volume and 93.7% of its excess velocity squared error fall in
the first wall-distance band (below 0.01 nondimensional, about 5 cm), and
over 99% within 2 m (results/v0_interior_excess_sse_2026-09-08.json,
reduced from the band artifact below); those are fractions of the error on
the near-wall-biased sample, not volume integrals, and the query-token
configurations have not been reduced this way. The far-field ratio growth
is real, and it is where a passive read of surface-centred slices has least
to go on, but the far bands carry a negligible share of the sampled error,
so "missing volumetric context" is a reading of the ratio panel, not a
measured cause. The interior sample is stratified by the unsigned distance
from each query to the full-resolution vehicle surface (the SDF magnitude),
into three bands fixed before the models were evaluated. The thresholds
are 0.4 and 4.0 in the recipe's nondimensional coordinates, which
DrivAerML's per-case reference length L_ref = 5 m (read from the
artifact by the figure code) converts to metres: *near* is less than 2 m
from the surface, *mid* 2–20 m, *far* beyond 20 m. In the passive arms'
gauge units (the constant gauge 8.0, 40 m physical) the same thresholds
are 0.05 and 0.5. The sampler's near-wall bias makes the bands very
unequal: 97.8% of points near, 2.0% mid, 0.12% far, so the far band holds
4–25 points per car. Within each band the per-car relative L2 is computed
over the band's points only and averaged over cars; @fig-interior-bands
plots each arm's ratio to GeoTransolver-volume, which the sampling bias
does not distort.

```{python}
#| label: fig-interior-bands
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Interior error relative to GeoTransolver-volume as a function of
#|   distance from the wall, for the passive-decode arms and the
#|   exact-kernel decoder (bfloat16 evaluation; every arm under one
#|   instrument, so the ratios stand). For each band, the per-car relative
#|   L2 is computed over that band's points and averaged over the 48 cars;
#|   the line is the ratio of two-seed means (arm ÷ GeoTransolver-volume)
#|   and the small markers are the paired per-seed ratios (filled = seed 42,
#|   open = seed 43, same x). Left, pressure; right, velocity including the
#|   freestream mean. Log axis. The hollow purple marker is the exact-kernel
#|   decoder's far-band pressure, whose output there is identically zero
#|   (see text); it is not evidence of accuracy. How to read this: a rising
#|   line means the arm loses more ground to GeoTransolver-volume as queries
#|   move away from the body. It does not show absolute error, which for
#|   pressure in the far band is dominated by a near-zero denominator, and
#|   it does not include the query-token arms. Data:
#|   results/v0_sdf_band_2026-09-05.json.
#| code-fold: true
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib as mpl
BLUE, RED, PURPLE = "#2a78d6", "#e34948", "#7b4fb3"
INK, INK2, MUTED, GRID, BASELINE = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#898781", "#e1e0d9", "#c3c2b7"
mpl.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 110, "font.size": 10, "axes.edgecolor": BASELINE,
                     "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID,
                     "xtick.color": MUTED, "ytick.color": MUTED, "xtick.labelcolor": INK2,
                     "ytick.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.spines.top": False,
                     "axes.spines.right": False, "legend.frameon": False})

band = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" / "v0_sdf_band_2026-09-05.json"))
scheme = "prereg_Lref8"
pa = band["per_arm"]["case_mean"]
bands = band["band_definitions"][scheme]["names"]
thr = band["band_definitions"][scheme]["sdf_thresholds_nondim"]
L_m = band["global_data_first_case"]["L_ref"][0]  # metres per nondimensional unit
frac = band["band_fractions"][scheme]
edges = [f"< {thr[0] * L_m:g} m", f"{thr[0] * L_m:g}–{thr[1] * L_m:g} m", f"≥ {thr[1] * L_m:g} m"]
def pct(f):
    return f"{100 * f:.2g}" if f < 0.01 else f"{100 * f:.1f}"
ticks = [f"{b}\n{e}\n{pct(frac[b]['case_mean'])}% of points" for b, e in zip(bands, edges)]
arms = [("ISLA passive, SDF-gradient normal", "mt2_int_sdf", BLUE, "-"),
        ("ISLA passive, proxy normal", "mt2_int", BLUE, "--"),
        ("exact-kernel decoder", "mt1k_vol", PURPLE, "-")]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.2, 4.2), sharey=True)
import math
for ax, field, title in zip(axes, ("pressure", "velocity"), ("pressure $C_p$", "velocity $U/|U_\\infty|$")):
    labels = []
    for name, key, color, ls in arms:
        g = [pa["gt_vol"][scheme][b][field] for b in bands]
        a = [pa[key][scheme][b][field] for b in bands]
        ratio = [ai["mean"] / gi["mean"] for ai, gi in zip(a, g)]
        ax.plot(range(3), ratio, color=color, ls=ls, lw=1.8, zorder=3)
        for i, (ai, gi) in enumerate(zip(a, g)):
            artefact = key == "mt1k_vol" and field == "pressure" and bands[i] == "far"
            for s_idx, mfc in enumerate((color, "white")):  # filled = seed 42, open = seed 43
                r = ai["seeds"][s_idx] / gi["seeds"][s_idx]
                ax.plot([i], [r], marker="o", ms=5 if not artefact else 8, ls="none",
                        mfc=mfc if not artefact else "white", mec=color,
                        mew=1.2 if not artefact else 1.6, zorder=4)
        labels.append([math.log10(ratio[-1]), name, color])
    # direct labels at the far band, pushed apart on the log axis where they would collide
    labels.sort()
    for j in range(1, len(labels)):
        if labels[j][0] - labels[j - 1][0] < 0.075:
            labels[j][0] = labels[j - 1][0] + 0.075
    for ly, name, color in labels:
        ax.text(2.08, 10 ** ly, name, color=color, fontsize=8.5, va="center")
    ax.axhline(1.0, color=RED, lw=1.2, zorder=2)
    ax.text(-0.35, 1.0, "GeoTransolver-volume", color=RED, fontsize=8.5, va="bottom")
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.set_xticks(range(3))
    ax.set_xticklabels(ticks, fontsize=8.5)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.3)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10, color=INK2, loc="left")
    ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
axes[0].set_ylabel("rel-L2 ratio, arm ÷ GeoTransolver-volume [–, log]")
axes[0].set_yticks([0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20])
axes[0].set_yticklabels(["0.5", "1", "2", "5", "10", "20"])
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

For ISLA with the SDF-gradient normal the pressure ratio runs 2.5x near,
3.7x mid, 3.3x far; velocity runs 2.3x near, 4.7x mid, 5.4x far. The
proxy-normal construction has the same shape (3.1x → 3.3x → 3.0x on
pressure, 2.5x → 4.5x → 6.4x on velocity). The near-wall band, where a
local-detail deficit would show first, is ISLA's *best* band on every
field. The reading is mechanical: ISLA's slices and anchors are
surface-centred and its read blocks consult slice states and boundary
tokens, so a query 10 m into the wake has nothing off-surface to read.
GeoTransolver-volume's interior tokens supply that context to each other.

Two cautions about the far band. It holds 573 points across the 48 cars,
so its ratios move by tens of percent between seeds (the SDF arm's far
velocity ratio is 6.4x on one seed and 4.4x on the other). And far-band
*pressure* relative L2 is a poor readout for every architecture,
GeoTransolver-volume included: 20 m from a car the true C_p has an RMS of
0.0055, so GeoTransolver-volume's absolute error of about 0.01 in C_p gives
it a far-band pressure relative L2 of 1.71, worse than predicting zero,
while its far-band velocity error is 0.021 |U_∞|. The 1.71 is a
denominator two orders of magnitude below the near-wall one, not an
engineering failure; the velocity panel, whose denominator is the
freestream, is the well-conditioned view of the far field.

## What does not work {#sec-interior-negatives}

Two mechanisms were tested as ways to give ISLA interior context or an
interior prior without giving up query independence. Both fail, for
different reasons: the first adds tokens that hurt, the second starts
from a physical prior that is worse than a constant on this flow.

### Latent volume tokens along anchor normals

**Latent volume tokens along anchor normals make the passive decode
worse, by 1.43x on pressure.** The construction: before the encoder,
each of the 256 slices has a geometric anchor (weighted mean position
z_s, mean normal m_s, and an RMS radius ρ_s of the points it owns). Three
tokens are placed off each anchor at z_s + c ρ_s m_s for c ∈ {0.5, 1, 2},
plus one at the centroid: 769 tokens whose positions are built
covariantly from the surface alone. They enter the slice routing as
interacting tokens with a separately learned measure weight and are
readable by interior queries through the ordinary read blocks; SE(3)
covariance and interior query independence survive. With the
SDF-gradient normal as base, the result on the 48 cars (bfloat16, both
arms under one instrument; results/v0_lvt_reduction_2026-09-07.json) is
pressure 0.228 against 0.160 without the tokens (0.233 / 0.224 against
0.166 / 0.153 by seed), velocity 0.371 against 0.308, eddy viscosity
0.581 against 0.372. The tokens did not fail to help; they hurt, on both
seeds. The likeliest reasons sit in the construction: 769 near-body tokens
with nearly identical invariant seeds enter the measure-weighted routing on
which the surface tokens rely, and offsets of 0.5–2 anchor radii never
reach the mid and far bands where the deficit is largest. The supported
statement is narrow: **off-surface latent tokens placed along anchor
normals, as interacting tokens in ISLA's routing, degrade the interior
decode.** The same tokens added to the interacting query-token
configuration make its far-wake eddy viscosity worse too
(@sec-interior-open).

### Why not an exact boundary-integral prior?

**The exact double-layer kernel is not a usable prior for separated
flow, so the flagship does not evaluate exact boundary-integral
kernels.** The question deserved asking: a boundary-integral decoder is
query-independent and exactly covariant by construction, and on linear
problems with exact labels the same decoder generalizes exactly across
boundary-condition content, which is why it was a candidate here; those
results are archived with the design. Three measurements on DrivAerML
answer it. The first is a zero-parameter
oracle: on the 45 of 48 validation cars whose remesh passes a
watertightness and Gauss-identity check, exact inviscid potential flow
(single- and double-layer integrals on the closed remesh, Neumann data
U_∞·n, second-kind solve, Bernoulli C_p) is evaluated at the recipe's
surface points and compared to the CFD pressure. Its measure-weighted
relative L2 is **4.8** (median 1.97, every car above 1.6); on the same
points, predicting C_p = 0 scores 1.00 and predicting each car's mean
C_p scores **0.77**. No numerical control rescues it (an oracle-optimal
affine rescale reaches 0.73; a remesh-resolution sweep is flat; the
solver is exact on a sphere to 0.07%). The physics is the reason: 69% of
a DrivAerML surface carries C_p in [−0.5, 0], the separated-base deficit,
where inviscid flow predicts roughly 0 to +0.13, and inviscid suction
peaks are two to three times too strong. A decoder built as "exact
Laplace kernel plus learned correction" starts from a field worse than a
constant.

The second is the trained exact-kernel decoder in @tbl-interior, at
**9.7x** GeoTransolver-volume on interior pressure with learned densities
on top of the exact kernels. The comparison is not resource-matched
(0.76M parameters at 4.0 GB against 27.6M at 8.8 GB). The caveat would
matter if more capacity could plausibly close the gap; the oracle says
otherwise, because the field the learned densities must correct is
already worse than a constant.

The third is the decoder's far-band behaviour in @fig-interior-bands. Its
far-band pressure ratio of 0.59x GeoTransolver-volume is not accuracy: its
far-field pressure output has decayed to identically zero (|C_p| below
10⁻⁶ on every far point, against a true RMS of 0.0055), which yields the
trivial relative L2 of 1.000 on all 48 cars and both seeds and beats
GeoTransolver-volume's 1.71 only through the denominator problem above. On
far-band velocity, the well-conditioned readout, the exact-kernel
decoder is **16.7x** GeoTransolver-volume (RMS velocity error 0.34 |U_∞|
against 0.027), and there is no distance band under any definition in
which the double-layer decoder is within 1.5x of GeoTransolver-volume on
velocity. The exact-kernel line is closed for separated
three-dimensional aerodynamics on every readout in this book.

## Standing and open designs {#sec-interior-open}

**One architecture covers the surface and the interior, and on the interior
it leads on one field of three. ISLA's reference configuration, query
tokens with the signed distance on the frame-free relative frame, is 27%
more accurate than GeoTransolver-volume on interior velocity (0.73x) at
8.9M parameters against 27.6M, with the two models' inputs matched, keeps
exact SE(3) covariance, and trails on pressure (1.07x) and eddy viscosity
(1.14x). Its passive decode is the configuration to use when interior
query independence is contractual, at 9.9M parameters, 4.9 GB and a 3.1x
price in interior pressure error.** The diagnostics that locate the two
deficits were run on the similarity-gauge variant, which matches the
reference on pressure and velocity and trails it on eddy viscosity (0.1142
against 0.1005 on the 10,000-cell boundary; the difference is not
attributed between the frame and the corrected boundary measure, which
changed together, @sec-nb-relint-verdict). They are read here as
statements about the interacting query-token configuration.

*Parameter budget.* At matched parameter count the pressure ordering
changes: the similarity-gauge variant at hidden width 344 (27.6M
parameters, GeoTransolver-volume's budget; exact recompute, two seeds)
scores 0.0497 / 0.0729 / 0.1033, leading GeoTransolver-volume on pressure
by 3% (0.97x) and on velocity by 32% (0.68x) and trailing on eddy
viscosity by 18% (1.18x, inside the preregistered inconclusive band
1.10–1.25). The interior-pressure ordering is therefore a parameter-budget
statement, behind at 8.9M and ahead at 27.6M, and width buys 9% / 8% / 7%
for 1.8x parameters at about 1.3x step time. An intermediate width of 256
(about 15.7M parameters) stands at 1.02x / 0.72x / 1.17x
(results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_interior_2026-09-09.json). The
eddy-viscosity gap that remains is carried neither by width nor by
GeoTransolver-volume's local features: GeoTransolver-volume without them
scores 0.0551 / 0.1111 / 0.0924, so the features are a 4–7% general
carrier, not the lead
(`research/transfer_program/studies/computational_support/campaign_d_verdict_2026-09-10.json`).

*Where the eddy-viscosity gap lives.* Splitting the saved float32
predictions of the two matched-parameter models by signed distance to the
wall, they are equal on eddy viscosity in the near-wall band (signed
distance below 0.01 body lengths, 77% of the points: 0.081 against 0.080),
ISLA leads in the mid band (0.062 against 0.077) and trails only in the far
field (at or beyond 0.05 body lengths, 10% of the points: 0.093 against
0.068), which carries 46% of ISLA's squared eddy-viscosity error against
36% of GeoTransolver-volume's. Pressure and velocity show the same
pattern: near the wall ISLA leads on both (0.049 against 0.051; 0.086
against 0.128), far from it GeoTransolver-volume leads (0.082 against
0.067; 0.040 against 0.033). Split further by distance shell, ISLA leads
GeoTransolver-volume on eddy viscosity everywhere within 0.4 body lengths
of the surface (0.047 against 0.067 at 0.05–0.1 L, 0.042 against 0.053 at
0.1–0.2 L, parity at 0.2–0.4 L), around the car (0.034 against 0.050) and
upstream (0.046 against 0.108); the entire deficit is the far wake beyond
0.4 body lengths downstream, 2.2% of the query points (0.108 against
0.071), worst beside the car. Pressure carries a uniform 15–25% deficit in
every far shell that does not grow with distance and holds under 2% of the
squared error. The sharper interior statement is therefore: at matched
parameters ISLA leads GeoTransolver-volume on pressure, velocity and eddy
viscosity everywhere except the far wake beyond 0.4 body lengths, which
carries the whole 18% eddy-viscosity deficit
(`research/transfer_program/studies/computational_support/band_decomposition_2026-09-10.json`,
`far_field_shells_2026-09-10.json`).

*What does not close it.* Three classes of remedy are tested and none
closes the far-wake gap. Anchor geometry: three interacting wake tokens on
the drive axis (over the rear deck, in the near wake and 0.7 body lengths
behind the car) close a fifth of the far-band eddy-viscosity gap (0.093 to
0.087 against GeoTransolver-volume's 0.068), within the reference's 14%
seed spread, and the latent-volume tokens along the surface normals make
the far band worse (0.110); neither moves the near-wall or mid band. A
routing-mass probe over all twelve blocks shows why the anchor reading was
misplaced: interior query tokens dominate 224–256 of the 256 slices in
every layer, so 48–86% of the anchors already sit off the surface, and
they follow the query mass, which is why few reach a wake that holds 2% of
the sample
(`research/transfer_program/studies/computational_support/band_decomposition_wake_2026-09-10.json`).
Training-time sampling: a measure-consistent oversampling of the far field
(inclusion probability rising with the signed distance, exact importance
weights recorded, far band raised from 10% to 32% of the training queries),
trained on two seeds and scored in float32 on the standard uniform sample,
makes every field worse in every band: far-shell eddy viscosity 0.193
against the reference's 0.118, recipe pressure +36%, velocity +22%, eddy
viscosity +48% (@sec-nb-farwake-verdict;
`results/farwake_far_field_shells_2026-09-11.json`). The arm trains the
interacting decode on one query distribution and scores it on another, so
part of that cost is the query-distribution dependence of
@sec-interior-companion and the arm cannot separate "not under-sampled"
from "swamped by the swap"; what it settles is that a training-time
sampling law is not a deployable remedy. Query-side inputs: ISLA-native
"local features", measure-weighted surface-patch integrals at three radii
around each query, leave eddy viscosity at 1.36x GeoTransolver-volume
(past the preregistered 1.25 falsifier) with pressure and velocity
unchanged within 1%; a scalar with the local density of queries within a
ball of radius 0.05 and a channel of invariants over each query's 16
nearest queries stand at 1.32x and 1.30x against 1.28x without either
(results/qtdens_reduction_2026-09-10.json, @sec-nb-qt-density-verdict).
Handing the model the sample density outright gains nothing, and both
density channels read the discretization rather than the physics, so they
are excluded from the flagship by the principle of @sec-principle
regardless of the result.

*Capacity.* A single-car training test sorts the three standings: with one
car presented as 64 resampled views, the single-car ratios to
GeoTransolver-volume are 1.25x on pressure, 0.67x on velocity and 1.64x on
eddy viscosity, against the same variant's full-data 0.92x, 0.65x and
1.30x under the same bfloat16 instrument. The velocity lead is unchanged
with the data fixed and is therefore capacity; the eddy-viscosity deficit
widens and is capacity too, so more training cars will not close it; and
the pressure standing reverses on one car, so what pressure lead the
variant has at full data is generalization across cars rather than
representation (@sec-nb-overfit-interior). The remaining
representational candidate for the far wake, that the downstream coordinate
enters the seed only implicitly, is not scheduled.

*Small data.* The standings are mostly full-data statements. Without the
signed distance, trained on 54 or 109 cars, GeoTransolver-volume leads the
query-token configuration by 1.3x on interior pressure (0.096 against
0.124 at 54 cars, 0.069 against 0.092 at 109; velocity 1.4x, eddy
viscosity 1.8x), a wider margin than the 1.2x by which it leads ISLA on
the DrivAerML surface below full data (@sec-de-drivaerml). With the signed
distance the pressure deficit is 1.19x at 54 cars, 1.18x at 109 and 1.07x
at 435, velocity moves from parity to an ISLA lead (0.94x at 54, 0.83x at
109, 0.73x at 435), and eddy viscosity stays 1.3–1.5x in
GeoTransolver-volume's favour throughout
(results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_interior_2026-09-09.json). The
eddy-viscosity gap, flat across an eightfold change in data with the
inputs matched, is what GeoTransolver-volume's parameters still buy. Two
qualifications bound it. The metric is on the standardized viscosity
(@sec-interior-task), so a ratio there is an ordering under that centering
and not a statement about physical viscosity error. And DrivAerML's closure
is a hybrid RANS/LES model whose modeled viscosity depends on a grid or
filter length, so a query's neighbours in the volume mesh carry
information about the discretization as well as about the flow; the null
of the density and neighbour channels above weakens the reading that
GeoTransolver-volume's local aggregation recovers discretization rather
than a physical wall feature, without ruling out a mechanism those
channels do not reproduce.

*The passive decode.* Neither construction of a query normal closes its
gap, the SDF gradient is the better of the two by 1.2x, and the distance
stratification shows the excess error concentrated at the wall with a
ratio that grows away from it (@sec-interior-distance); a
request-independent probe set that would supply interior context while
keeping the passive decode is a design, not a result, and is not pursued
while the query-token configuration leads on velocity. The exact-kernel
decoder is not a contender on this task. @sec-limits collects the interior
limits alongside the book's others.
